Package index

The interface

One call per analysis, cv.bregsurv(target, release, divergence, ...): the target model built from your data, the release the external source made, and the divergence through which the release enters. cv.bregsurv() chooses the integration weight (and the penalty) by cross-validation; bregsurv() fits at a given weight.

Fitting

cv.bregsurv()
Fit a time-to-event model that borrows from an external source
bregsurv()
Fit a time-to-event model that borrows from an external source, at a given weight

Step 1: the target

The model you fit to your own data. It sets the likelihood of the objective.

target_cox()
Target: a Cox model
target_ncc()
Target: a nested case-control design
target_discrete()
Target: a discrete-time model
nn_score()
A neural-network risk score

Step 2: the release

What the external source made available. Its form decides which divergences can use it.

release_records()
Release: individual records
release_coef()
Release: a fitted model, with or without its uncertainty
release_score()
Release: a risk score without survival probabilities
release_model()

Predictions from a fitted model

Estimators: the composite likelihood (individual-level records)

The external cohort’s records are available. The generator is the negative external log-likelihood, so the objective is a composite likelihood in which the external records carry weight eta and each cohort keeps its own baseline. One family per design, each fit with a cv. counterpart that chooses eta (and lambda) by cross-validation.

Estimators: the Mahalanobis distance (coefficients with their uncertainty)

The external source released coefficients, and possibly their precision. The generator is a quadratic form, so the penalty is the Mahalanobis distance to the external coefficients, weighted by the precision matrix Q; with Q = NULL it is the Euclidean distance on the covariates the external model covers.

Estimators: the Kullback-Leibler divergence (a fitted model or a risk score)

Only the external model’s predictions are needed: a risk score (RS) or coefficients (beta) for a Cox or matched target, absolute risks (hazard, or beta with baseline) for a discrete-time target. The generator is the negative entropy on the distributions the model predicts, so the penalty is a Kullback-Leibler divergence. coxkl_ties also offers Cox’s exact method for tied event times; every full-cohort estimator accepts ties = "breslow".

Several external sources

One integration weight per source, in one fit.

coxkl_enet.multi()
Multi-Source Integration for KL-Integrated Cox Elastic-Net Models

Preparing the external information

Match a named external coefficient vector (and its precision matrix) to your covariates by name; absent covariates are set to zero. The fitting functions call these for you when beta is named.

align_beta()
Align an external coefficient vector to the internal covariate space
align_beta_Q()
Align an external coefficient vector and weighting matrix for MDTL

Choosing the integration weight

generate_eta()
Generate a Sequence of Tuning Parameters (eta)
bopt.coxkl()
Bayesian Optimization for the Cox–KL Integration Parameter (eta)
cv.plot()
Plot Cross-Validation Results vs Eta

Evaluating a fit

Score fixed coefficients, such as the external model used unchanged, on the same cross-validation folds as the fitted models, or on held-out data.

vvh_loss_fixed()
Cross-validated Verweij and van Houwelingen loss at a fixed coefficient vector
test_eval()
Evaluate Survival Model Performance
